text:
alex: Observed a regression on the sparse expert routing path — token shuffle across GPUs spiking tail latency. root cause looks like repeated large fanout during routing + non-overlapped NCCL comms.
priya: Saw the same on canary yesterday, p95 jumped ~2.3x after the kernel selector change. stack: pipeline parallel + expert shuffle.
jordan: Dumped traces, here's the hotspot: lots of short kernels then a blocking ncclAllToAll/AllReduce. compute idles waiting for comm.
lisa: Can you paste the trace snippet?
jordan: Sure, trimmed nvtx timeline:
```
[0.00s] kernel: fused_gemm_qkv_fp16 (18ms)
[0.018s] kernel: attention_softmax (4ms)
[0.022s] nccl: expert_shuffle_alltoall (65ms)  <-- big
[0.087s] kernel: output_proj_fp16 (12ms)
[0.099s] idle waiting for nccl (40ms)
```
alex: That long alltoall is the killer. Looks like kernel selector pushed a non-streamed kernel variant that synchronizes. Also KV cache behavior: hot prefix cache causes uneven sequence lengths per sample so fanout distribution is skewed.
priya: Where did the kernel selector change land? I remember a TTL that prefers 'fused_all' kernels for short sequences.
:jordan: It landed in the runtime branch that bumped heuristics for small batch/short seq to avoid repeated launches. But that fused_all variant uses a blocking stream sync to ensure correctness with packed KV layout.
lisa: So two issues: blocking kernel variant + imbalanced fanout due to KV cache/prefixing. Both amplify the NCCL cost.
perf-bot: Canary metrics: endpoint /generate-sparse-experts p95 latency 278ms -> 610ms after selector rollout, tail tokens/sec down 42%.
alex: Quick mitigation candidates: 1) revert selector to non-blocking kernel; 2) enable comm/compute overlap by launching NCCL ops on a dedicated stream and using async memcpy for shuffle; 3) add routing pre-shard pass to reduce cross-node fanout; 4) temporary batching heuristic that groups by cached-prefix length.
priya: I prototyped #2 yesterday — using NCCL async and CUDA events to overlap reduced p95 by ~30% in local tests. But still suffers when expert fanout > 128MB per GPU.
jordan: For #3, if we enforce routing affinity per microbatch (pin tokens to local-expert clusters) we can reduce all-node fanout but risk quality shift. Need eval.
lisa: Also, we should audit kernel selection logic: add a fast path that guarantees non-blocking for any variant used in distributed routing. Might be lighter change than full revert.
alex: Agreed. Action items: priya to land async-nccl experiment behind a flag; jordan to run quality-eval for routing-affinity on small prompt sets; lisa to add a selector test ensuring variant stream-safety; I'll open a short rollback PR if async doesn't stabilize canary by EOD.
priya: Starting feature flag PR now, will add perf results + script to reproduce with --fixed-seed.
jordan: I'll run evals on the 10k prompt suite and compare token-level KL and response length; if delta < 0.5% we can try affinity sharding.
lisa: Adding selector validation tests to runtime CI (check stream sync calls, kernel attribute).
alex: One more note — batching heuristics: if we bucket by prefix-length and enforce max-seq dispersion per batch, we reduce per-batch fanout variance. Might cost a bit of queueing delay but decrease comm spikes. Worth experimenting.
priya: I'll wire a bucketing mode in the batching config and test latency vs throughput tradeoff.
jordan: For observability, let's add per-request NCCL byte counts and expert fanout histogram to tracing so we can correlate.
lisa: Put the new metrics in console under model->routing so SRE can set alerts.
perf-bot: Stated task checklist created: EXPERT-ROUTE-REG-180234 (async-nccl, selector-test, routing-affinity-eval, batching-buckets).
alex: Great — ping here when you have a canary build. Also adding a short doc snippet for root cause so postmortem is easier if rollback needed.
priya: Will share perf logs and canary IDs in this thread. :thumbsup:
jordan: If we get async overlap working, next up is trying NCCL topo-aware grouping to limit cross-switch traffic.
lisa: Noted. thanks everyone.
